subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service disable for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override generated service-env and state-dir `.env` values, or should those persisted sources remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: This decides a sensitive diagnostic logging boundary across multiple operator-controlled env sources, and automation should not encode that precedence without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat `unset`, `0`, `off`, and `false` as authoritative for managed-service disable, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and generated service env authoritative, and document that operators must remove or edit those persisted values before restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor-Guided Repair
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add status/doctor checks that warn and repair stale raw-stream service-env values before operators believe logging is off.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat `unset`, `0`, `off`, and `false` as authoritative for managed-service disable, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The raw-stream runtime and service-env precedence surfaces both route through recent work and committer history tied to this area.
